text: Tell me about your school.
Niambie kuhusu shule yako.
Sọ fún mi nípa ilé-ìwé rẹ.
What did you do yesterday after school?
Ulifanya nini jana baada ya shule?
Kí ni o ṣe lánàá lẹ́yìn ilé-ìwé?
How do you get from your home to the market?
Unafikaje sokoni ukitoka nyumbani kwenu?
Báwo ni o ṣe ń lọ sí ọjà láti ilé?
What is your favourite subject, and why?
Somo gani unalipenda zaidi, na kwa nini?
Ẹ̀kọ́ wo ni o fẹ́ràn jùlọ, kí ló sì dé?
Tell me about a time you helped someone.
Niambie wakati ulipomsaidia mtu.
Sọ fún mi nípa àkókò kan tí o ran ẹnìkan lọ́wọ́.
Count out loud from one to twenty.
notes: Numbers are the strongest code-switch trigger in the classroom register -- which number form a speaker reaches for is an empirical result we want, not something to prompt for. Number register: prompt_sw uses standard Swahili number words (moja...ishirini); prompt_yo uses standard Yoruba number words (ọ̀kan...ogún). Neither uses digits or English, so the question itself doesn't prime an English or digit response.

text: What is 15 plus 7? Tell me how you worked it out.
notes: Same reason as prompt 6 -- arithmetic answers are where code-switching to English numbers is most likely to happen spontaneously, and that switch pattern is exactly what this set exists to capture. Number register: prompt_sw uses standard Swahili number words (kumi na tano, saba); prompt_yo uses standard Yoruba number words (mẹ́ẹ̀ẹ́dógún 'fifteen', èje 'seven'). Yoruba's numeral system is genuinely complex (base-20, subtractive forms for many numbers) -- flag this row for extra-careful native-speaker check, higher uncertainty here than the other rows.

text: Tell me something that happened at school this week.
Niambie jambo lililotokea shuleni wiki hii.
Sọ fún mi ohun kan tó ṣẹlẹ̀ ní ilé-ìwé ní ọ̀sẹ̀ yìí.
What do you want to do when you grow up?
Unataka kuwa nini ukikua?
Kí ni o fẹ́ ṣe nígbà tí o bá dàgbà?
Explain a game you play with friends, and its rules.
Nieleze mchezo unaocheza na marafiki zako, na kanuni zake.
Ṣàlàyé eré kan tí o ń ṣeré pẹ̀lú àwọn ọ̀rẹ́ rẹ, àti òfin rẹ̀.
